testing_note: Wrote scratch/notes1.md (a product sync with a suggested-but-unconfirmed pricing change, an agreed launch date later challenged, an ownerless task, relative deadlines and an unanswered question) and walked the draft skill's steps over it by hand. The walk-through showed the draft had no rule for a decision challenged later without resolution, so I added the 'contested decision' kind and the '(contested, see C1)' marker in the format; vague owners like 'someone' also prompted the rule to copy them as written and mark them unconfirmed.
applied_note: I made the skill model-invoked with a short description that front-loads 'decision brief' and names one trigger per branch (decisions, action items, open questions, handoff). The body puts the ordered steps first, each ending on a checkable completion criterion, with the final Check step carrying an exhaustive bar; the kind definitions and output format sit as co-located in-file reference since every run needs them, so no disclosed files were warranted. Leading words ('traces', 'unresolved', 'contested') carry the no-guessing rule positively instead of through prohibitions.
